record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Is a polygon secure if and only if it is almost integrable, meaning that it is covered by reflections of one of the integrable polygons whose associated flat surface is a flat torus?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a (compact, simply connected) polygon, and consider the billiard flow on $P$: trajectories travel along straight lines and reflect at the boundary according to the law of equal angles, with vertices excluded.

For two interior points $x,y\in P$, a finite set $B\subset P\setminus\{x,y\}$ is said to block all billiard trajectories from $x$ to $y$ if every billiard trajectory in $P$ starting at $x$ and ending at $y$ passes through some point of $B$. The polygon $P$ is called secure if for every pair of distinct interior points $x,y\in P$ there exists a finite blocking set $B$ for the trajectories from $x$ to $y$.

A polygon $P$ is called integrable if it is one of the polygons whose associated translation (flat) surface, obtained by the Zemlyakov–Katok unfolding construction, is a flat torus; equivalently, $P$ is one of the square, the equilateral triangle, the right isosceles triangle, or the $30^\circ$–$60^\circ$–$90^\circ$ triangle. A polygon $P$ is called almost integrable if it is tiled by reflections (in its sides and their iterates) of an integrable polygon.

Question: Is it true that a polygon $P$ is secure if and only if $P$ is almost integrable?
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence "secure iff almost integrable" for polygons is a well-known conjecture (often attributed to Gutkin) that appears still open in general. One direction (almost integrable implies secure, and partial results for rational polygons) is known, and recent work (e.g., on weak mixing in rational billiards, 2024) has resolved related Gutkin-type conjectures characterizing almost integrability dynamically, but the full security characterization for arbitrary polygons does not appear to be settled.

status_evidence.title: Billiard dynamics: An updated survey with the emphasis on open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A polygon is secure if and only if it is almost integrable... almost integrable polygons are certainly rational... would imply that every irrational polygon is insecure.
status_evidence.claim: The statement is recorded as a conjecture in a recent survey of open problems in billiard dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Weak mixing in rational billiards (arXiv:2410.11117)
status_evidence.snippet: Complete classification of rational polygons whose billiard flow is weakly mixing in almost every direction, proving a longstanding conjecture of Gutkin; characterized as those which are not almost integrable.
status_evidence.claim: A related Gutkin conjecture characterizing almost integrability via weak mixing has recently been proved, but this is not the same as the security conjecture.
